project_impact_alignment.title: Advancement of European AI agent technology to global leadership position
project_impact_alignment.mechanism: MAESTRO's neuro-symbolic planning (WP2), adaptive memory (WP3), and formally verified coordination (WP4) establish a European-origin paradigm for trustworthy AI agents, with the open-source framework (WP8/WP9) enabling European researchers and companies to build on these advances without dependency on non-European platforms.

impact_pathways.impact_narrative: MAESTRO directly advances AI agent model architecture, memory management, and autonomous reasoning capabilities through three integrated research pillars: the neuro-symbolic planning engine (D2-01, D2-02) delivers formal sub-task graph decomposition and MCTS/HTN-LLM integration; the adaptive tri-store memory system (D3-01, D3-02) enables coherent long-horizon agent behaviour without retraining; and the tool orchestration layer (D8-01) provides typed tool selection policies and auditable invocation traces. These advances are consolidated in the integrated MAESTRO framework (D8-02) and open-source release (D9-02), directly unlocking AI agent potential across economic sectors in alignment with the Apply AI Strategy.

impact_pathways.impact_narrative: MAESTRO contributes to the Apply AI Strategy through three sector-validated demonstrators deployed via EDIH networks and validated in Testing and Experiment Facilities. dissemination_plan.open_access_policy: All MAESTRO peer-reviewed publications will be made openly accessible in compliance with Horizon Europe open access mandates. Accepted manuscripts will be deposited in open repositories (e.g., arXiv, institutional repositories, or publisher open access portals) immediately upon acceptance, with gold or green open access routes applied as appropriate. Research data underpinning publications will be made FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) and deposited in appropriate domain repositories or Zenodo, as specified in the Data Management Plan (DMP) deliverable due within the first 6 months of the project. The open-source MAESTRO framework (D9-02) and benchmark suite (D8-03) will be released under a permissive open-source licence (Apache 2.0 or equivalent) to maximise reuse by the European R&D community and SMEs. Software and datasets contributed to the AI-on-demand platform will comply with the platform's open access and interoperability requirements.

exploitation_plan.ipr_strategy: MAESTRO adopts a differentiated IPR strategy aligned with the project's dual objectives of European open strategic autonomy and commercial exploitation. Core research outputs — including the neuro-symbolic planning engine, adaptive memory architecture, and formally verified coordination protocols — will be assessed for patentability by consortium technology transfer offices at M24 and M42. Where patent protection is pursued, it will be filed by the generating partner(s) with consortium-wide licensing rights to ensure all partners can exploit the technology. The open-source MAESTRO framework (D9-02) and benchmark suite (D8-03) will be released under a permissive open-source licence (Apache 2.0 or equivalent), deliberately excluding core patentable innovations from the open-source release to preserve commercial exploitation pathways. Sector-specific demonstrator outputs (clinical decision support, manufacturing optimisation, logistics) will be subject to joint ownership agreements where multiple partners contribute, with exploitation rights allocated by sector to the partner with the strongest commercialisation capacity in that domain. All IPR decisions will be governed by the Consortium Agreement, which will include provisions for background IP protection, foreground IP allocation, and access rights for exploitation purposes.

sustainability_mechanism.description: MAESTRO's post-project sustainability is ensured through four complementary mechanisms that maintain the availability, development, and impact of project results beyond the grant period. First, the open-source MAESTRO framework (D9-02) will be maintained as a community-governed open-source project under a designated stewardship organisation (the coordinator institution or a purpose-established European AI foundation), with a governance model established by M48 to ensure continued development, security patching, and community engagement beyond M60. Second, the EDIH network integration (≥3 EDIHs actively disseminating MAESTRO technology by M48) provides an institutionalised channel for continued technology transfer to European SMEs and startups beyond the project lifetime, with EDIHs incorporating MAESTRO tools into their standard service portfolios. Third, the clinical decision support and manufacturing demonstrators are designed for post-project commercial adoption: the clinical validation pathway (HTA body acceptance by M48) and manufacturing technology transfer agreements (≥5 SMEs by M48) create revenue-generating exploitation routes that sustain the technology without continued public funding. Fourth, the standardisation submission to ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 42 or IEEE (by M48) embeds MAESTRO's formally verified coordination protocols into international standards, ensuring long-term relevance and adoption independent of the project consortium. The AI-on-demand platform hosting of the benchmark suite (D8-03) provides persistent infrastructure for scientific community access, maintained by the platform operator beyond the project end.
